title: CloudFront CDN
description: Learn how Amazon CloudFront distributions, origins, cache behaviors, and S3 work together for fast content delivery.

data.text: A Content Delivery Network (CDN) is a network of servers spread across the globe that cache copies of your content. When a user requests your content, the CDN serves it from the server closest to the user. This reduces latency, improves load times, and reduces the load on your origin server.

data.title: How CloudFront Works
data.text: CloudFront caches content at edge locations around the world. When a user requests content, CloudFront serves it from the nearest edge location if available. If not cached, CloudFront fetches it from the origin, caches it, and then delivers it to the user.

A CloudFront distribution is the configuration container for your CDN. It defines where your content lives (the origin), how it is cached (cache behaviors), and how it is secured (TLS settings, signed URLs, geo-restriction). Each distribution gets a unique domain name like d1234.cloudfront.net.

An origin is the source of the content that CloudFront distributes. Common origins include S3 buckets, EC2 instances, and Application Load Balancers. A cache behavior defines how requests are routed to an origin based on the URL path pattern. You can have multiple cache behaviors with different origins.

data.title: Key Cache Behavior Settings
items: Path Pattern — Which requests match this behavior (e.g., /images/*).
Origin — Where the cached content comes from.
Viewer Protocol Policy — Whether to allow HTTP, HTTPS, or redirect HTTP to HTTPS.
TTL — How long CloudFront caches content before checking the origin for updates.
Allowed HTTP Methods — Which HTTP methods are forwarded to the origin.

data.text: A common pattern is to store static assets in an S3 bucket and distribute them through CloudFront. S3 stores the originals, and CloudFront caches copies at edge locations. This gives you the durability of S3 combined with the low-latency delivery of a global CDN. You should also use an Origin Access Control (OAC) to restrict direct S3 access to CloudFront only.

The source location of the content, such as an S3 bucket or load balancer.
Rules that determine how CloudFront routes requests to origins and caches responses.
A data center that caches copies of your content close to users.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: CloudFront is AWS's global content delivery network
Distributions define how content is cached and delivered
Origins are the source locations for your content
Cache behaviors control routing based on URL patterns
S3 + CloudFront is a common pattern for static websites and assets
